# ADR-1087: Install sqlite-vec unconditionally on every plugin install

## Status

accepted

## Context

The SQLite backend is Cortex's zero-config default (`scripts/install-plugin.sh`). Its vector (semantic) search depends on the `sqlite-vec` SQLite extension, declared in `pyproject.toml` only under the `[sqlite]` optional-dependencies extra.

Neither of the two dependency-install paths the plugin actually uses ever named that extra:
1. `scripts/launcher_pins.py::BASE_PACKAGES` — installed by `scripts/launcher_deps.py::ensure_deps()` on every hook/session-start launch — listed `psycopg`/`psycopg_pool`/`pgvector` (the `postgresql` extra) unconditionally, but nothing from `[sqlite]`.
2. `requirements/setup.txt`, generated by `scripts/generate_pip_constraints.py` from the extras `("postgresql", "codebase", "benchmarks")` (`scripts/pip_constraint_sets.py`) and installed by `scripts/setup.py::install_deps()` on **both** backends (`SKIP_POSTGRES` does not change which requirements file is read).

Consequence (issue #634): the SQLite backend ran with vector search silently disabled on every install, on every OS — `doctor`/`check_setup` reported the store fully ready regardless. This is wider than a Windows-specific bug: the pin lists are identical on every platform.

## Decision

Install `sqlite-vec` unconditionally, the same way `psycopg`/`pgvector` (the PostgreSQL drivers) are already installed unconditionally regardless of the chosen backend — one universal dependency set is simpler than branching the install path per backend, and it means a later `install-plugin.sh --postgres` upgrade never needs a second dependency pass to also gain SQLite vector search.

Concretely: add `"sqlite"` to `pip_constraint_sets.py`'s `setup.txt` `ConstraintSet.extras` (and add `scripts/setup.py` to its `consumers`, since it silently already read this file), regenerate `requirements/setup.txt`; add `("sqlite_vec", "sqlite-vec==0.1.9")` to `launcher_pins.py::BASE_PACKAGES`, pinned to the same version.

## Consequences

Every install — SQLite or PostgreSQL, plugin or PyPI `[sqlite]` extra, existing or new — gets a working `sqlite-vec`. Existing installs self-heal on next launch, with no user action: `ensure_deps()`'s pin-satisfaction check compares `sorted(pins)` against a stamp file, so adding a new pin invalidates the stamp and triggers exactly one incremental `pip install` of the missing package (`_dist_info_satisfies` per-package check means only `sqlite-vec` itself installs, not the whole set).

Cost: PostgreSQL-only installs now also carry the small, dependency-free `sqlite-vec` package they will never load (`SqliteMemoryStore` is not constructed on that backend) — negligible size, matches the existing precedent of PostgreSQL drivers being installed unconditionally too.

Companion fixes (same issue, not this ADR's decision but recorded here for the reader): `SqliteMemoryStore.select_fallback_embeddings`'s re-embed worklist now also matches rows with a non-empty `embedding_model` but no corresponding `memories_vec` row (a vector computed but never persisted because sqlite-vec was absent at write time), so such rows self-heal once the extension becomes available — previously only the `embedding_model='fallback'` label was matched, and a correctly-labelled `'neural'` row with no vector could never resurface. `doctor`/`check_setup` gained an optional vector-search check distinguishing "package not installed" from "installed but this Python's sqlite3 cannot load extensions" (different fixes: reinstall vs. a different Python build). The `embedding_upgrade` consolidation cycle now reports `vectors_persisted: 0` alongside `upgraded: N` when the store cannot persist vectors at all, so "upgraded" is never misread as "N vectors written".
